text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports a painful, red big toe that has worsened over about two weeks, especially after prolonged standing or walking.
- history of present illness: intermittent big toe pain for about two weeks, markedly worse last week during a trade show, with throbbing and sharp pain on movement and at night under bedsheets; no known injury; redness and warmth prompted the visit; ibuprofen (about two tablets daily) has not helped.
- physical examination: pain with dorsiflexion and plantarflexion (limited to about 10–20 degrees), pain and grinding on first metatarsophalangeal joint motion, tenderness on medial and lateral sides, bone spur palpated; x-ray shows a large dorsal spur and loss of joint cartilage consistent with hallux rigidus.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: throbbing and sharp big toe pain, redness, warmth, pain with pressure from bedsheets, difficulty walking, and altered gait (walking on the heel).
- new medications prescribed or changed: meloxicam once daily (dosage not specified); orthotic shoe insert.
- follow-up instructions: return in two weeks to assess improvement; stop meloxicam and call if heartburn or epigastric pain develops; continue regular work and activities; if no significant improvement, consider injection or surgery (joint cleanup or fusion).
